close_reason:
Rewrote ChatWsFrame::Unknown.type_name rustdoc to enumerate all four sources of the field's String value:
1. Verbatim @type string from underlying WsFrame::Unknown
2. '<no @type>' (jmap-base-client's own sentinel for absent @type)
3. 'ChatTypingEvent' / 'ChatPresenceEvent' (known-chat-event payload deser failure)
4. '<unknown>' (future non-Unknown base-client WsFrame variants)

Verified all four sources by reading crate-jmap-base-client/src/ws/mod.rs:300 (origin of '<no @type>' literal) and chat-client ws.rs:48-71 (the parse_chat_ws_frame match arms). Bead's analysis of the doc/impl mismatch was solid.

Bead's suggested follow-up of a typed UnknownKind enum is deferred — that's a larger API-shape change not in scope for this doc fix.

rustdoc -D warnings clean. cargo test green. Committed as 11ed5d8.
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-client/src/ws.rs:36 (doc) vs :69 (impl).

Line 36 documents:
```
/// The `@type` value from the JSON frame; `"<no @type>"` if absent.
```

Line 67-71 (the only place this crate constructs `ChatWsFrame::Unknown` with a synthetic value):
```rust
_ => ChatWsFrame::Unknown {
    type_name: "<unknown>".to_owned(),
},
```

A caller reading the doc would write defensive code matching `frame.type_name.as_str() == "<no @type>"` to detect "absent @type" cases. This will never match for any frame this crate produces — they get `"<unknown>"` instead.

The base-client's own `WsFrame::Unknown` may produce `"<no @type>"` internally (per `jmap-base-client`'s contract), but `parse_chat_ws_frame` only falls into this branch for *non-Unknown* base frames it doesn't recognise — i.e. for future variants of `jmap_base_client::WsFrame` — which is the `"<unknown>"` case. The base-client's own `WsFrame::Unknown` flows through one of the other arms (lines 53-65 or 67-68), so the `<no @type>` literal from the base never actually lands in `ChatWsFrame::Unknown.type_name`.

Fix: align the doc with the impl. Either:
- Change the doc to: `"\"<unknown>\" when the base WsFrame variant is not recognised by this parser, or the verbatim @type string from the base WsFrame::Unknown otherwise."` (depends on what the base actually produces — verify with jmap-base-client's `WsFrame::Unknown` doc).
- Or change the impl to `"<no @type>".to_owned()` to make the literal match. The doc is the more useful contract; the impl literal is internal.

Compounding issue: the field has two distinct semantic meanings packed into one `String` (parser-saw-unrecognised-variant vs server-omitted-@type), which makes the contract awkward regardless of the literal chosen. A typed `ChatWsFrame::Unknown { kind: UnknownKind }` enum would be cleaner but is a larger change.
title: ChatWsFrame::Unknown.type_name doc says "<no @type>" but impl produces "<unknown>"
